name: codecash
description: codecash has paused ad serving. This update turns off ad injection and restores your original Claude Code settings. Accrued earnings remain available to cash out at codecash.dev.

contributes._commandsNote: SUNSET BUILD: only the two commands that still mean something are LISTED here. The other six (connect/enable/signIn/signOut/shareEarnings/contactSupport) are still REGISTERED in src/sunset.ts so an existing keybinding or a palette-history invocation resolves to the sunset notice instead of throwing 'command not found' — they're just no longer advertised. The old commandPalette `when` clauses were removed with them: they keyed on contexts this build never sets, which would have hidden 'Disable' while leaving 'Connect & start earning' visible.

codecash: Restore my Claude Code settings

codecash.enabled.description: Inject ads into the Claude Code spinner + status line. Managed by codecash: Enable / Disable — you normally don't edit this directly.

codecash.apiBaseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of the codecash server this extension fetches ads from and reports events to. Leave blank to use the build default (`http://localhost:3000` for local builds). Changes take effect on the next ad fetch.

enumDescriptions: Generic ads. codecash sends no information about your project.
Ads matched to your stack — you earn the premium rate.
codecash.relevantAds.markdownDescription: **Relevant ads — earn more.** When set to `relevant`, codecash derives ~a dozen coarse tags (e.g. `fw:next`, `lang:typescript`) from your workspace's manifest files (package.json, go.mod, Dockerfile, …) and sends **only those tags** so advertisers can match your stack. It **never** sends your code, file or repo names, paths, or prompts. Off by default; change takes effect on the next ad fetch.

codecash.codexSurfaces.markdownDescription: **Experimental — earn on OpenAI Codex too (off by default).** When on, codecash also shows ads on Codex's surfaces: a one-line banner on the `codex` CLI at launch, and (if the Codex VS Code panel is installed) a small ad pill in the panel while it's *thinking*. Unlike the Claude Code surfaces, Codex exposes no official hook, so these reach it by wrapping the `codex` PATH binary and patching the Codex panel extension on disk — both fully reversible (restored on Disable), but more fragile (a Codex update can revert the panel patch until the next reload) and potentially against those tools' terms. Leave off unless you've opted in deliberately. Requires a build with Codex surfaces compiled in.
